title: Re-argue ADR-002 AWS Glue rejection on F2 grounds, not cross-ADR consistency
description: ADR-002 line 77 rejects AWS Glue Schema Registry partly on the basis that 'Cloud dependency is inconsistent with ADR-001's self-hosted posture'. That is not an F2 criterion — F2 is GDPR/DORA/PSD2 fit. The actual F2 grounds are present in the same cell: data residency requires explicit EU region configuration (GDPR), and DORA resilience testing is not under operator control on a SaaS. Lead with those concrete regulatory grounds; drop the cross-ADR consistency clause. The current framing risks circular reasoning — Glue fails because other ADRs picked self-hosted, not because the regulatory filter actually fails it.

title: Replace ambiguous 'Pass (note: ...)' verdicts in F2 tables with explicit conditional-pass labelling
description: Multiple ADRs use 'Pass (note: mitigation required)' in F2 hard-filter tables: ADR-001 (RabbitMQ, NATS), ADR-002 (Avro), ADR-005 (Valkey, OpenSearch, DuckDB), ADR-007 (Jaeger). When a 'Pass' requires a substantive mitigation clause, it is effectively a conditional pass — the current label is ambiguous because the verdict column has to either lie ('Pass') or carry a footnote. Two options: (a) add a third 'Conditions' column with clean Yes/No verdicts, or (b) use 'Pass*' with the asterisk explained beneath the table. Pick one convention and apply it series-wide.

title: Reconcile Karapace placeholder in ADR-008 P6 with chosen Redpanda SR (ADR-002)
description: ADR-008 P6 (around line 328) uses '<karapace-registry-url>' in the AsyncAPI $ref example. ADR-002 explicitly chose the Redpanda built-in schema registry (which exposes the Confluent SR API). Karapace is a separate implementation and is not mentioned anywhere in ADR-002. Replace the placeholder with '<schema-registry-url>' (neutral) or '<redpanda-sr-url>' (specific). Cross-ADR placeholder inconsistencies make a reader question whether the rest of the series has been reconciled.

title: Add ADR-006 placeholder or renumber to close sequence gap
description: ADR-000 line 7 references 'ADR-001 through ADR-010' but the actual files are 001, 002, 003, 004, 005, 007, 008. The gap at 006 is unexplained and reads as carelessness. Either renumber subsequent ADRs so the sequence is contiguous, or add a one-line ADR-006 stub explaining 'reserved / deferred / superseded by X'. Whichever option is chosen, update the ADR-000 'Applies to' scope statement to match. This is the single most important fix in the editorial review — a missing number in an ordered decision log undermines confidence in the whole series.
close_reason: Duplicate of existing planned-ADR tracking: archie-guz (ADR-006: Edge API gateway) is already in the archie-9ci epic, so the sequence gap is intentional, not a deletion. Writing ADR-006 will close the gap naturally; the ADR-000 scope statement update can be handled inside whichever issue authors ADR-006.

title: ADR-000: Common evaluation criteria for all tool selections
description:
Define the shared evaluation template that every ADR (001–010) will apply. Produces a reusable criteria rubric and a short prose section that each ADR includes by reference.

## Why this exists

Each ADR will evaluate different tools against different functional requirements, but a set of cross-cutting criteria applies to all of them. Defining these once avoids drift between ADRs and forces each decision to be honest about the same hard constraints.

## Budget constraint

**Budget is effectively 0€.** This is a first-class filter, not a soft preference. It means:
- Managed cloud services (Confluent Cloud, Datadog, Temporal Cloud, AWS MSK, etc.) are disqualified unless they have a genuinely usable free tier with no credit-card-required production cliff.
- Self-hosted open-source is the default mode.
- Tools with open-core models are acceptable only if the features required by the architecture sit in the free/community tier — the ADR must explicitly verify this.
- Licensing traps (BSL, SSPLv1, ELv2, Commons Clause) must be flagged even if currently free, because they constrain future use.

## Criteria to define

1. **Cost / licensing** — total cost of self-hosting (infra, ops time) vs free tier limits; licence type and change risk.
2. **Regulatory fit** — GDPR (data residency, right to erasure), DORA (resilience testing, RTO/RPO documentation), PSD2 (audit trail, SCA). Hard pass/fail before functional comparison.
3. **Operational complexity at small scale** — how much ops burden does this add to a small team? Preference for tools that degrade gracefully when not actively tuned.
4. **Ecosystem coherence** — does it compose with the rest of the chosen stack without bespoke glue? Native OpenTelemetry, standard connectors, etc.
5. **Exit cost** — how painful is migration away in 3–5 years? Does the tool own a data format or protocol that creates lock-in?
6. **Community and longevity** — is this tool likely to still be maintained in 10 years? Red flags: single-vendor control with recent licence change, stagnant commits, small contributor base.
7. **Functional fit** — tool-specific criteria defined per ADR.

## Deliverable

A markdown section titled '## Common Evaluation Criteria' usable as a template block in each ADR, plus a summary rubric table (criteria × weight) that each ADR fills in for its candidates.
acceptance_criteria: Template section written and agreed. Each ADR-001–010 issue updated to reference this template.

title: ADR series: tool selection for integration implementation
description: A conversation-driven ADR series covering every major technology decision needed to move the integration_concepts documents into working software. Each child issue drives one focused conversation and produces one ADR in markdown. Acceptance: all child ADRs written and committed.

title: Editorial pass on ADR-008 (event catalog governance)
description: Three edits (Karapace placeholder tracked separately): (1) Line 91 'Governance tooling that nobody uses is not governance' is the strongest line in the entire series; promote it from the Git-native rejection sub-section into the Decision section as a load-bearing claim. (2) Line 167 residual risk on EventCatalog commercial tier — list which features today are open-source vs paid so a future re-evaluation has a baseline. (3) P3 tombstone contract SerDe configuration string ('value.deserializer.null.value.default = true') — verify currency against the actual Confluent Avro SerDe library version that will be used. Code-shaped configuration strings date fastest.

title: Editorial pass on ADR-007 (observability stack)
description: Four edits: (1) Lines 38–46 candidate table includes Datadog as a row but Zipkin is excluded in a free-standing paragraph beneath; pick one exclusion convention (table row with 'Excluded before evaluation' OR free-standing prose) and apply series-wide for consistency with ADR-005's MongoDB exclusion. (2) Line 73 Jaeger F2 is currently 'Pass (note: RBAC gap)'; given the financial-data context, reconsider as 'Fail unless mitigated' — in a regulated context the burden of mitigation is the headline, not a parenthetical. (3) Line 175 residual risk on Grafana Labs commercial trajectory — list which observability-critical features are currently OSS vs Enterprise so a future re-evaluation has a baseline. (4) P4 attribute tier example 'deposit.client_id = CLI-2026-007842' already looks pseudonymous; pick an example that contrasts raw vs pseudonymous more obviously (raw NIF vs opaque token) so the contrast lands.

title: Editorial pass on ADR-005 (CQRS read model storage)
description: Three edits: (1) Line 52 MongoDB exclusion claim 'No substitute document store offers sufficient community and ecosystem support to merit evaluation' is too strong — CouchDB (Apache 2.0) and ArangoDB community edition exist. Replace with a narrower claim: 'No substitute open-source document store materially out-performs PostgreSQL for the projection patterns at this scale.' (2) Consider adding a fourth upgrade trigger to the Decision section: what would cause a wholesale revisit rather than per-projection introduction of a specialised paradigm — e.g., 'if measured read SLA exceeds budget across three or more projections simultaneously, re-evaluate the single-storage assumption.' (3) Line 196 materialised view refresh-overlap risk — name the failure mode plainly ('two overlapping refreshes contend for the materialised view's lock; both stall') rather than the abstract 'creates overlap'.

title: Editorial pass on ADR-004 (outbox pattern)
description: Three edits: (1) Line 173 residual risk first says CDC 'conflicts' with polling then immediately explains they don't (Debezium ignores the status column). Reword the first sentence to name the actual risk: 'Running both mechanisms simultaneously causes duplicate publication during the cutover window; consumer inbox dedup will absorb it, but the migration sequence below avoids it entirely.' (2) Line 244 'before the buffer grows to a problematic size' — reference the P4 thresholds (30s warning / 5min critical) so the residual risk has a measurable trigger. (3) Line 232 cleanup query — clarify that the 7-day retention is the *outbox delivery record* operational retention, not the audit trail (the Redpanda topic is the audit source). Otherwise a compliance reader will read 'delete after 7 days' and worry.

title: Editorial pass on ADR-003 (saga orchestrator)
description: Three edits: (1) Line 23 has a long parenthetical of saga states (STARTED, PARALLEL_VALIDATION, ... CANCELLED) inside a context sentence; promote to a bulleted list or footnote — currently hard to scan. (2) Lines 57–58 Temporal and Conductor F2 table cells run multiple sentences of analysis; compress to verdict-plus-footnote (related to the conditional-pass labelling issue). (3) Line 70 verify the Temporal services list ('Frontend, History, Matching, Worker, Internal Frontend') against the current Temporal version — 'Internal Frontend' is a newer split and not present in all releases; either cite the version or generalise to 'multiple internal services in production deployments'.

title: Editorial pass on ADR-002 (schema format and registry)
description: Two edits (AWS Glue framing tracked separately): (1) Line 187 promote the CloudEvents envelope-vs-payload distinction from a multi-sentence bullet to its own Consequence bullet — currently a reader can miss that the schema registry manages only the business payload, not the envelope. (2) Line 199 residual risk on 'Redpanda built-in SR feature surface' — name the specific features to verify (context-namespaced schemas, schema export, schema references). The current text says 'verify before relying on any non-standard SR capability' which is unactionable without a list of what to look at.

title: Editorial pass on ADR-001 (event backbone)
description: Five edits: (1) Line 16 opening paragraph has three em-dashes and a parenthetical clause — break into two sentences for prosody. (2) Line 58 RabbitMQ F2 cell runs four sentences of analysis; move the prose to soft criteria and keep only the verdict in the cell (related to the conditional-pass labelling issue). (3) Line 69 'Redpanda's developer mode (--mode dev-container) starts in seconds' — strike 'trivially' from related claims; say 'simple'. (4) Line 152 'S3-backed infinite retention' overstates — use 'extended retention via S3' or 'tiered storage with much longer retention'. (5) Line 87 'Pulsar's market position has not grown as fast as Kafka's since 2020' — anchor the observation date (refer to ADR header date 2026-05-17).

title: Editorial pass on ADR-000 (common evaluation criteria)
description: Three edits: (1) Line 19 'Effectively zero' is the only soft phrase in an assertive opening — replace with a definitive constraint statement (e.g., 'Zero' or 'Bounded to free tiers and self-hosted OSS'). (2) Line 39 F1 acceptable licence list '(Apache 2.0, MIT, GPL, LGPL, AGPL)' reads as exhaustive but ADR-001 accepts MPL 2.0 for RabbitMQ; either prefix with 'e.g.' or rewrite to 'OSI-approved permissive or copyleft licence that does not restrict use in financial services'. (3) Line 75 S4 'stagnant commit activity or declining community' needs a heuristic threshold (e.g., commits from non-founding contributors in the trailing 12 months) so future ADRs do not re-derive it. (4) Update line 7 scope statement once ADR-006 status is settled.

title: Clarify ADR-007 'Proposed' status with review timeline
description: ADR-007 (observability stack) is the only ADR with status 'Proposed'; all others are 'Accepted'. Per commit log this is intentional (pending review), but a reader landing on ADR-007 cold cannot tell whether 'Proposed' means 'open for debate' or 'filed and forgotten'. Add a one-line note under the status field: 'Pending review by [name] before acceptance; expected by [date].' This makes the intent visible without changing the decision.

title: ADR-010: Anti-corruption layer implementation approach
description: Decide the implementation pattern for the ACL between the domain and Core Banking (doc 02). Conversation topics: dedicated ACL service vs sidecar vs library; adapter patterns for SOAP/XML ↔ domain events; polling adapter vs webhook vs MQ bridge depending on Core capabilities; failure isolation — bulkhead and circuit-breaker placement; how ACL state interacts with the outbox (ADR-004). Deliverable: ADR-010.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.

title: ADR-009: Testing infrastructure and contract testing
description: Decide the testing tools for the strategy in doc 07 — component, integration, contract, and saga tests. Conversation topics: Pact vs OpenAPI contract testing vs schema-registry compatibility checks; Testcontainers for Kafka and DB integration tests; saga test harness — replaying events against the orchestrator in isolation; chaos/resilience testing (DORA requirement, doc 10); test data management for a GDPR-regulated system. Deliverable: ADR-009.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.

title: ADR-008: Event catalog governance tooling
description: Decide the tooling for maintaining the event catalog and schema governance described in doc 08. Conversation topics: AsyncAPI as the specification format; EventCatalog vs Backstage vs Confluent Control Center vs custom portal; ownership model and review gates tied to the schema registry (ADR-002); breaking-change detection automation; integration with CI/CD. Deliverable: ADR-008.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.
notes: ADR-002 consequence: the event catalog conventions must document that Avro SerDes on compacted topics must be configured to tolerate null payloads (GDPR tombstones). Consumers that enforce a non-null Avro schema will crash on compaction tombstones. This is a per-topic contract requirement — document it as a standard field in the catalog entry for any event on a compacted topic.

title: ADR-007: Observability stack
description: Decide the distributed tracing, metrics, and logging tools for the observability model in doc 06. Conversation topics: OpenTelemetry as the instrumentation baseline (traces, metrics, logs); Jaeger vs Tempo vs Zipkin for trace backends; Prometheus + Grafana vs Datadog vs Elastic APM; correlation of trace IDs with the identity trio (doc 01 — correlation/causation IDs); GDPR-safe logging — what can be stored and for how long (doc 10). Deliverable: ADR-007.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.

title: ADR-006: Edge API gateway and synchronous layer
description: Decide the API gateway and edge technology for the synchronous REST/JSON layer described in doc 00 (the sub-500ms boundary). Conversation topics: Kong vs AWS API Gateway vs custom BFF per channel (web/mobile/branch); how the gateway enforces PSD2 SCA (doc 10); rate limiting and circuit-breaking at the edge; SSE/WebSocket push for optimistic UI status updates; integration with the identity/auth layer. Deliverable: ADR-006.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.

title: ADR-005: CQRS read model storage
description: Decide the storage technology for the materialized read models described in doc 03. Conversation topics: PostgreSQL projections vs Elasticsearch vs Redis vs dedicated read DBs per bounded context; write throughput from event replay; query flexibility vs operational simplicity; how the ACL (doc 02) feeds Core Banking data into these projections; cache invalidation and eventual consistency UX implications. Deliverable: ADR-005.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.

title: ADR-004: Outbox pattern mechanism
description: Decide the technical mechanism for implementing the outbox pattern (doc 04 — the non-negotiable primitive for dual-write safety). Conversation topics: CDC-based outbox via Debezium vs polling publisher vs library-embedded outbox (Eventuate Tram, Axon outbox); connector reliability and lag SLAs; database compatibility (PostgreSQL assumed); interaction with idempotency and inbox deduplication. Deliverable: ADR-004.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.
close_reason: ADR-004 written and accepted: custom polling publisher chosen; Debezium upgrade path documented in Consequences

title: ADR-003: Saga orchestrator
description: Decide the saga orchestration engine for complex multi-step flows (constitution, early mobilization, maturity renewal) described in docs 00 and 05. Conversation topics: Temporal vs Conductor vs Axon Framework vs rolling a custom orchestrator on top of the message broker; durable execution vs explicit state machines; how the orchestrator holds saga state and drives compensations; operational footprint and observability integration (doc 06). Deliverable: ADR-003.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.
close_reason: ADR-003 accepted: custom event-driven application orchestrator chosen over Temporal/Conductor/Axon

title: ADR-002: Schema format and registry
description: Decide the serialization format and schema registry for all integration events. Doc 04 and 09 name Avro and Protobuf as candidates alongside a schema registry, but the choice is not made. Conversation topics: Avro vs Protobuf vs JSON Schema — compatibility rules, tooling, language support; Confluent Schema Registry vs AWS Glue Schema Registry vs Apicurio; forward/backward/full compatibility strategies tied to doc 09 evolution patterns; impact on the event catalog (doc 08). Deliverable: ADR-002.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.
close_reason: ADR accepted: Avro + Confluent SR API + Redpanda built-in SR for POC

title: ADR-001: Event backbone — message broker choice
description: Decide which message broker to use as the event backbone. The integration_concepts series assumes Kafka in a greenfield context (doc 00, 04), but the decision must be explicit and justified. Conversation topics: Kafka vs Pulsar vs RabbitMQ (streams mode) vs NATS JetStream; durability guarantees; topic compaction and retention for event sourcing; operational complexity in a Portuguese banking context; managed vs self-hosted. Deliverable: ADR-001.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.
close_reason: ADR written, CDC scoping clarified, committed and pushed

title: Cross-cutting editorial sweep across ADR series
description: Apply consistent edits across all ADRs as a single pass: (1) Audit and strike 'trivially/trivial' usages — if it is trivial, the word is unnecessary; if it is not, the word is wrong. (2) Replace softener phrases ('effectively zero', 'effectively open') with the actual constraint. (3) Audit 'may/should' inside Implementation Principles sections (ADR-003 through ADR-008); principles are normative, so prefer 'must' or declarative present tense. (4) Reduce em-dash density in opening paragraphs and dense analytical passages — three em-dashes per paragraph reads as nested asides. (5) Anchor all relative date phrases ('since 2020', 'as of 2026') to the ADR header date or a specific calendar date.
